keys.description: Show first-run setup on startup. Missing or true shows onboarding; continuing from onboarding writes onboarding = false.

Update channel used by background version checks and herdr update. Stable Windows builds default to stable; existing Windows preview installs stay on preview until explicitly switched. Homebrew, mise, and Nix installs ignore the preview channel.

Modifier that lets right-click gestures pass through to pane apps. Empty disables it. Accepts ctrl, alt, cmd, super, meta, hyper, or a + separated combination; shift is rejected because many terminals reserve Shift+mouse.
Force a full host-terminal redraw when the outer terminal regains focus.

Draw borders around split panes.

Draw interactive scrollbars beside terminal panes. Disable to reclaim the scrollbar column and keep it out of terminal-native selections.
Keep split panes visually separated instead of sharing divider borders.
Override color for the focused (active) pane border. Same syntax as `accent`. Unset uses the theme accent.
Override color for unfocused (inactive) pane borders. Same syntax as `accent`. Unset uses the theme's muted border color.
Box-drawing weight for the focused pane border: "light", "heavy", or "double".
Override color for the focused pane's border title. Same syntax as `accent`. Unset follows `pane_border_active_color`, then the theme accent.
Override color for unfocused panes' border titles. Same syntax as `accent`. Unset follows `pane_border_inactive_color`, then the theme's muted color.
Show a todo indicator at the far right of a split pane's top border, carrying the pane's outstanding todo count.

Override color for the pane todo indicator while todos are outstanding. Same syntax as `accent`. Unset colors it by the highest outstanding priority (high red, normal yellow, low blue); an all-done indicator is always muted.

Default background for the focused pane's cells (tmux `window-active-style` bg). Same syntax as `accent`. Only cells without an explicit app-painted background are tinted. Unset keeps the terminal default.
Default background for unfocused panes' cells (tmux `window-style` bg). Same syntax and semantics as `pane_active_bg`.
Dim unfocused pane content in all modes, not only while a herdr mode (prefix/navigate) is active.
Show agent labels in split pane borders when no manual pane label is set.
Hide the tab row when the workspace has one tab.
Place the desktop tab row above or below the terminal panes.
Configure ordered right-aligned tab bar entries. Supported types are zoom, hostname, datetime, text, and command.
Text inserted between visible right-aligned tab bar entries.
Title Herdr writes to the terminal it runs in. Tokens: {hostname}, {workspace}, {tab}, {pane}, {terminal_title}. Empty leaves the outer title alone.
Agent sidebar ordering. Saved values are "spaces" or "priority"; "workspaces" is accepted as an alias for "spaces".
Choose compact color dots or distinct static symbols for agent states.
Working icon motion in sidebar agent rows: `on` steps a spinner on a slow shared tick while any agent is working; `off` keeps the static working glyph.
Milliseconds between working-spinner frames, clamped to 50..=2000.
Milliseconds the `prefix+i` labels and the resize labels stay up, clamped to 500..=60000.
Blank terminal rows between expanded Agent sidebar entries. Set to 1 to restore the previous spacing.

Default expanded Agent sidebar layout. Entries may be token strings or inline { token, fg, bold, dim, italic, keep, truncate } style tables. Supports built-in and $name metadata tokens; at most 16 rows and 16 tokens per row.
Complete Agent-row overrides keyed by strict canonical agent id. Agents without an override use ui.sidebar.agents.rows.
Blank terminal rows between worktree groups and unrelated top-level Spaces. Worktree parents and their indented children remain packed.

Expanded Space sidebar layout. Entries may be token strings or inline { token, fg, bold, dim, italic, keep, truncate } style tables. Supports built-in and $name metadata tokens; at most 16 rows and 16 tokens per row.
Show the workspace jump symbol (1-9, then a-z; the `switch_workspace` target) on the sidebar branch line.
Show each agent's jump symbol (1-9, then a-z; the `focus_agent` target) on the agent panel status line.
Show the herdr server's short host name, right-aligned on the sidebar "SPACES" header row.
Color for `show_workspace_numbers` labels. Same syntax as `accent`. Unset uses the theme's muted number color.
Color for `show_agent_numbers` labels. Same syntax as `accent`. Unset uses the theme's muted number color.
Leader glyph(s) shown before the workspace jump number when sidebar_style is "editorial", e.g. "₽" to hint the prefix+N chord. Rendered in workspace_number_color. Empty leaves the bare number.
Leader glyph(s) shown before the agent jump number when sidebar_style is "editorial", e.g. "₽⌥" to hint the prefix+alt+N chord. Rendered in agent_number_color. Empty leaves the bare number.
Sidebar workspace list ordering. "manual" keeps the user's drag order, "priority" bubbles attention-needing workspaces to the top.

How priority-sorted lists (spaces, agents panel) apply reorders. "bubble" holds a row in place for `sort_motion_settle_ms`, then moves it one position per `sort_motion_step_ms` so the list never teleports under the cursor; "instant" re-sorts immediately.
How long a row holds its position after its sort position changes before it starts bubbling, in milliseconds.
Interval between one-position bubble steps, in milliseconds.

Step cadence across a reshuffle. "linear" spaces every step evenly; "bubble" eases in and out — slow to break away, quickest mid-flight, slowing into the final slot. The curve stretches over the reshuffle, so it only reads as acceleration when rows travel several positions.
Sidebar entry composition. "default" keeps the current layout; "editorial" right-aligns jump numbers on the name row, renders thin uppercase section headers, and dims inactive meta lines.
Color for working state glyphs and state text (spinner, working dot). Same syntax as `accent`; unset follows the theme.
Color for idle (finished and seen) state glyphs and state text. Same syntax as `accent`; unset follows the theme.
Color for done (finished, unseen) state glyphs and state text. Same syntax as `accent`; unset follows the theme.
Color for blocked state glyphs and state text. Same syntax as `accent`; unset follows the theme.
Color for unknown state glyphs and state text. Same syntax as `accent`; unset follows the theme.
Color for agents parked at their prompt while work they launched keeps running (state glyph and state text). Same syntax as `accent`; unset follows `working`.
Glyph for the working state icon. Exactly one terminal cell wide; unset keeps the glyph from `ui.status_indicators`.
Glyph for the idle (finished and seen) state icon. Exactly one terminal cell wide; unset keeps the glyph from `ui.status_indicators`.
Glyph for the done (finished, not yet seen) state icon. Exactly one terminal cell wide; unset keeps the glyph from `ui.status_indicators`.
Glyph for the blocked state icon. Exactly one terminal cell wide; unset keeps the glyph from `ui.status_indicators`.
Glyph for the unknown state icon. Exactly one terminal cell wide; unset keeps the glyph from `ui.status_indicators`.
First frame of the pulse drawn for an agent parked at its prompt while work it launched keeps running. Exactly one terminal cell wide; unset keeps the built-in glyph.
Second frame of that pulse; the two swap once per four spinner ticks. Exactly one terminal cell wide; unset keeps the built-in glyph.

Notification center position. "top-right" puts the indicator in the tab bar with the dropdown under its right edge; "bottom-right" floats the indicator in the frame's bottom-right corner with the dropdown opening above it.

Highlight pattern for the active space and agent in the sidebar, using `pane_border_active_color` and `pane_border_active_style`. Accepts "off", "above", "below", "both", "left", "right" — or a bool for backward compatibility (true = "both"). "left"/"right" also apply in the collapsed sidebar, which reserves one extra edge column for the bar; "above"/"below"/"both" draw nothing there (no spacer rows).

How the spaces list and the agent panel show rows scrolled out of view. "rows" puts a dim summary row at an edge with rows hidden past it (`↑ 2 pinned · 3 more` above, `↓ 5 more · ● 1 blocked` below; click it to scroll a page toward it). "fog" lifts the background of the two rows next to that edge, the nearest the most, toward the text colour, with a faint tint of the most urgent hidden state; the focused and selected rows never fog. "both" does both, "off" neither. Reloads live.

How far the `sidebar_overflow` fog lifts the two rows next to a hidden edge, in percent of the way from the background to the text colour, nearest row first. 0 to 2 entries, each clamped to 0..=60 with a diagnostic; 0 (or a missing entry) means no fog on that row. Reloads live.
How much of the most urgent hidden state's colour (blocked, or finished and unseen) the fog takes, 0..=100, clamped with a diagnostic. 0 keeps the fog neutral. Reloads live.

What the `sidebar_overflow` fog does: `lift` (a lighter background), `dim` (the text of the fogged rows fades toward the background, three times the row's `sidebar_fog` percent, at most 90, by recolouring rather than the terminal dim attribute) or `both`. An unknown value is reported and uses `lift`. Reloads live.
Accent color for highlights, borders, and navigation UI. Accepts hex (#89b4fa), named colors (cyan, blue), or RGB (rgb(137,180,250)).
Popup notification delivery. off disables popups, herdr shows in-app toasts, terminal asks the outer terminal for a desktop notification, system asks the OS notification service directly.

Seconds to wait before sending finished or needs-input agent notifications. Herdr notifies only if the pane is still in the same state when the delay expires. 0 is instant; valid values are 0 through 3600.
In-app toast position, relative to the full Herdr frame.
Toast box size preset: "auto" hugs the text, "medium" and "large" widen the box relative to the anchor area.
How long a needs-attention toast stays visible, in seconds. 0 keeps it visible until clicked or replaced.
How long a finished toast stays visible, in seconds. 0 keeps it visible until clicked or replaced.
How long an update-installed toast stays visible, in seconds. 0 keeps it visible until clicked or replaced.

Where notes about a pane action (a refused pane move, a failed clear scrollback or todo save) show: "corner" uses the position above, "pane" centers them in the pane acted on and falls back to the corner when that pane is not in view or is too small.
Show the copied-to-clipboard popup after a mouse copy.

Copied-to-clipboard popup position. "pane" centers it in the pane the text came from (a mouse or copy-mode copy, or an app's OSC 52 write) and falls back to bottom-center when that pane is not in view or is too small.
Play sounds when agents change state in background workspaces.
Optional mp3 file path used for all notification sounds. Relative paths are resolved from the config file's directory.
Optional mp3 file path for "done" notifications. Relative paths are resolved from the config file's directory.
Optional mp3 file path for "request" notifications. Relative paths are resolved from the config file's directory.

Sound override for detected Maki agents.
Resume supported AI-agent panes into their native conversation sessions when restoring a Herdr session.

Milliseconds between automatic agent restores after a server restart. The first agent starts without this delay; 0 disables spacing. Does not delay manual launches or explicit terminal attaches. Restart the server to apply.

Launch and resume Codex panes on the shared Codex app-server daemon: herdr adds `--remote unix://<app_server_socket>` and `-C <pane cwd>` to `agent start --kind codex` and to restored `codex resume`. Arguments you pass yourself win. Unix only.
The Codex app-server daemon's control socket. `~` expands to your home directory.
Name each Codex pane's daemon thread after the pane's agent name, and rename it when the agent is renamed. Needs `agents.codex.app_server`. Ephemeral threads are skipped.
Root directory under which Herdr creates <repo>/<branch-slug> checkouts.
Add keepalive fallbacks and private connection reuse for `herdr --remote`. Set false to run plain ssh unchanged.
Maximum scrollback buffer size in bytes retained per pane terminal. The legacy key name `scrollback_lines` is accepted as an alias.
Allow launching herdr inside an existing herdr pane.
Experimental local Kitty graphics rendering for attached clients.
Persist pane screen history to session-history.json.

Expose the focused pane's cursor anchor to the outer terminal even when the pane requested `?25l`, so macOS native input methods keep tracking the candidate window when TUIs paint their own cursor (Claude Code, pi, codex, etc.). Default: false.  When the pane reports no cursor position, falls back to the pane's top-left so a stable IME anchor is always available.  Trade-off when enabled: an extra hardware cursor will be visible in the outer terminal for apps that hide the cursor without painting a replacement (vim normal mode, etc.). See #149.

Restrict `reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime` to focused panes whose detected agent matches one of these names (case-insensitive). Empty list means apply to any focused pane. Unknown agent names are ignored; if the list contains no valid names, the reveal does not apply. Accepted names: pi, claude, codex, gemini, cursor, devin, cline, opencode, copilot, kimi, kiro, droid, amp, grok, hermes, kilo, qodercli, qoder, qwen, qwen-code, maki.
Cursor shape rendered for the IME anchor when `reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime` is enabled.

While prefix mode is active, temporarily switch the host input source to an ASCII-capable mode so prefix commands are read as ASCII even when an IME is active, then restore the previous input source when prefix mode exits. On macOS this selects the ASCII-capable keyboard layout; on Windows it switches the IME to English (ASCII) input. Windows support is currently limited to the Korean IME; with an IME for any other language, the input source is left unchanged. macOS and Windows only; a no-op elsewhere and a best-effort no-op if the switch fails.
